Analysis by Richard Cowan  

 

Ordinarily, the collapse of some hack’s political campaign would be off-topic for MarijuanaNews.com, but there is a lesson to be learned from the media’s treatment of Rudy Giuliani’s failed Presidential bid. 

 

Both the Establishment punditocracy and the Progressive blogosphere missed the real Giuliani story, because they are afraid even to think about how marijuana prohibition really works, much less write about it.  

 

Giuliani was often portrayed as a “social liberal” because as mayor of New York City he was “gay friendly” and supported “abortion rights.” But those were the politically safe positions that were necessary to get him the support of the “liberal” New York Times. However, there was – and to a large degree still is – another side of the Times that Giuliani courted. He was their hit man in the Drug War. 

See

Transcript of 1996 Conversation Between the Czar and the Former Managing Editor of New York Times About Medical Marijuana Initiatives Gives Great Insight Into How Marijuana Prohibition Really Works. 

And some things have not changed at The Times. 

See

New York Times Cheers "MEXICO TO JOIN US IN FIGHT ON DRUGS – Treaty is expected to cut down smuggling across border and break up gangs of dealers." We Couldn’t Make This Up! 

In any case, Giuliani was certainly the right man for their job. Before he was elected marijuana arrests in the City were rare, because New York is actually a “decrim” state. According to NORML, the first two offenses for possession of 25 grams or less is a “civil citation” with no jail time. All that changed when he became mayor.

See 

Marijuana Arrests In New York City Continue to Soar. Arrests Will Exceed 60,000 for this Year. Up From Only 720 in 1992! 

 

At a Central Park vigil to commemorate the life of John Lennon on the 20th anniversary of his murder, New York police arrested 19 people for smoking marijuana. There were over 60 uniformed police -- plus enough undercover narks to arrest 20 people -- at this, the most peaceful of gatherings.  

 

Giuliani commented, "It is illegal in the United States of America to sell or smoke marijuana. The police were doing what they should be doing." 

 

These arrests were a part of NYPD’s grandiosely named “Operation Condor”, which paid about 1,000 narcotics and patrol cops overtime, but felony drug arraignments actually dropped 8%. They went after casual marijuana users, instead. 

 

The experience of a friend’s son was typical. The boy in his late teens was offered some marijuana by an undercover nark, and was then busted. He was handcuffed and put in the backseat of the police car, and had to sit there for a few hours while they looked for someone else to arrest. Then, late in the day he was finally taken to the police station, but it was too late to book him so he was held overnight in jail. Fortunately, he was not assaulted and did not catch any of the diseases prevalent there. His parents got him out the next day.  

 

Of course, I realize that the ever-so-serious people who hyperventilate about conditions at Guantamo could never take the arrest of tens of thousands of Americans seriously. It might threaten their social status. But if they had not been afraid to look, they might have learned something. Rudy Giuliani has always been a fraud. He is given credit for things he did not do, and has escaped blame for the horrible things that happened in his city for which he was responsible. 

See 

Giuliani’s Police State – Like the Marijuana Prohibition That He Loves – Is A Counterproductive Fraud. 3 Articles. 

New Yorkers deserve better, and many of them know better. 

See 

Cannabis Friendly Cities Rank Highest In International Quality of Life Survey. For personal safety, “Lowest scoring city in North America is Washington D.C” Lessons for Civic Leaders. Special Report.
